name: Ilulissat Art Museum (Ilulissat Kunstmuseum)
overview: One of Greenland's two small art museums, with Nuuk Kunstmuseum, in Ilulissat (lex.dk).

It opened on 15 August 1995 as Greenland's first art museum. It began under Ilulissat Museum, which handed over a collection centred on the painter Emanuel A. Petersen; the two museums separated in 2004, when the art museum got its own head (lex.dk).
The house was built in 1923 as the colony manager's residence, designed by Helge Bøysen-Møller (ilulissatmuseums.gl, Visit Greenland, Scan Magazine).
funding_verdict: Ilulissat Art Museum: public: Avannaata Municipality

name: Kassák Múzeum
overview: Museum of the Hungarian avant-garde in the Zichy Castle, Fő tér 1, in Óbuda, Budapest. It is a member institution of the Petőfi Literary Museum (PIM) and has operated in the castle since 1976 (stated by the museum).

Named for Lajos Kassák (1887 to 1967), the Hungarian avant-garde writer, visual artist and editor whose material and intellectual heritage it preserves, researches and presents (stated by the museum).
Directors: Ferenc Csaplár (1976 to 2006), Gábor Andrási (2006 to 2010), Edit Sasvári (2010 to 2020) and Merse Pál Szeredi (2020 to the present).
funding_verdict: Kassák Múzeum: public: part of the Petőfi Literary Museum, with National Cultural Fund and German foundation support for projects
wider_context: Protest at the parent body: on 2 December 2020 artists and researchers held a demonstration in front of the Petőfi Literary Museum, organised by aHang, demanding the resignation of its director Szilárd Demeter after his Origó article comparing Europe to "George Soros's gas chamber", which he later withdrew. More than 28,000 people had signed the open letter calling for his resignation (444.hu, Szurovecz Illés, "Művészek és kutatók tiltakoztak Demeter Szilárd ellen a Petőfi Irodalmi Múzeum előtt", 2 December 2020; title translated: artists and researchers protested against Szilárd Demeter in front of the Petőfi Literary Museum).

State money for the foundation: hvg.hu reported on 17 February 2022 that a government resolution published in the Magyar Közlöny and signed by Viktor Orbán gave the Magyar Kultúráért Alapítvány, which it ties to Demeter, more than 48 billion forints over four years, from about 12.73 billion in 2022 to about 11.28 billion in 2025 ("Demeter Szilárd alapítványát 48 milliárd forintnyi közpénzből erősítik meg"; title translated: Szilárd Demeter's foundation will be reinforced with 48 billion forints of public money). The article refers to the Zichy Castle.

Neither piece names the Kassák Museum. The connection: the museum is a member institution of the Petőfi Literary Museum, and the Magyar Kultúráért Alapítvány maintains its building (museum's building page).

name: Kling & Bang
overview: Non-profit, artist-run gallery in the Marshall House at Grandagarður 20, in Reykjavík's harbour district, a former herring factory built in 1948 partly with US Marshall aid (City of Reykjavík announcement, 12 February 2016).

Founded in 2003 by ten local artists on Laugavegur in downtown Reykjavík. Founding member Erling Klingenberg said there was no platform for young or emerging artists to exhibit (The Art Newspaper, Tom Seymour, 15 November 2023). The article also names Hekla Dögg Jónsdóttir and Guðmundur Oddur Magnússon as founders of Klink and Bank.

The National Bank of Iceland contacted the gallery in November 2003, and the artists persuaded it to fund the conversion of an unused former fish-net factory nearby into a roughly 5,000 sq. m space called Klink and Bank. About 137 artists, designers, filmmakers and musicians worked there daily. The building was demolished in autumn 2006 (The Art Newspaper).
funding_verdict: Kling & Bang: artist-run non-profit: a city-guaranteed lease, TBA21 programme support and early support from the National Bank of Iceland

name: 1 Shanthiroad Studio Gallery
overview: Art space with a gallery and artist residencies at 1 Shanthi Road, Shanthinagar, in central Bengaluru.

Founded by Suresh Jayaram, a professor of art history and later dean at Karnataka Chitrakala Parishad from 1993 to 2007 (Temporary Art Review, 2015). The space's own site gives 2002 as the founding year, and the 2015 Temporary Art Review interview says it formally opened in 2002.
Run by the not-for-profit Visual Art Collective (VAC) Trust.
funding_verdict: 1 Shanthiroad Studio Gallery: mainly self-funded by the founder, with project grants for particular residencies and programmes

name: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Mumbai City Museum
overview: City museum in Byculla East, near the Byculla Zoo in Jijamata Udyan (Rani Baug), Mumbai (Wikipedia).

The idea dates to about 1850 and the 1851 Great Exhibition in London. The present building was built from 1862 to 1871, with David Sassoon, Sir Jamsetjee Jejeebhoy and Jagannath Shankarseth among its funders, and opened on 2 May 1872 as the Victoria and Albert Museum, Bombay (Wikipedia).
Renamed on 1 November 1975 for Dr. Bhau Daji Lad, a physician, philanthropist, historian and Mumbai's first Indian Sheriff (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad Mumbai City Museum: public-private partnership: Mumbai municipal corporation, the Jamnalal Bajaj Foundation and INTACH

press_items.title: Outlook News Desk, "Passage To Bombay" (page dated 5 February 2022)
FPJ Bureau, "Separate panel for Lad museum soon" (31 May 2019)
Girish Shahane, "Why the Shiv Sena and its cousin want to undermine the good work at Mumbai's BDL museum" (2015)

name: Khoj International Artists' Association
overview: Autonomous not-for-profit contemporary arts organisation at S-17, Khirkee Extension, New Delhi, across from Select Citywalk (stated by Khoj).

Founded in 1997. The founding working group was Ajay Desai, Anita Dube, Bharti Kher, Subodh Gupta, Prithpal Singh Ladi, Manisha Parekh and Pooja Sood, and Sood is currently its director (Wikipedia). Khoj's story page says the idea began as "a gift of possibility given by Robert Loder", founder of the Triangle Arts Trust.

The first workshop in 1997 brought 22 artists together in Sikribagh near Modinagar (Wikipedia). In 2002 Khoj acquired a building in Khirkee Extension. It reopened refurbished to the public in 2013 (Khoj's story page).
funding_verdict: Khoj International Artists' Association: donor-funded: foundations, cultural institutes and private donors

name: Gudskul (ruangrupa / Serrum / Grafis Huru Hara)
overview: Collective learning space for art at Jl. Durian Raya No. 30A, Jagakarsa, South Jakarta. The nearest rail stations are Ragunan (Transjakarta) and Lenteng Agung, each about a 30-minute walk or a short motorbike taxi ride (Gudskul contact page).

The collectives ruangrupa (founded in 2000), Serrum (2006) and Grafis Huru Hara (2012) formed Gudang Sarinah Ekosistem in 2015 and transformed into Gudskul in 2018 (Sharjah Art Foundation; Wikipedia).
Building: Gudskul owns land and a building, which an essay co-written by Gudskul says continue to be used "suboptimally" (e-flux, April 2026).
funding_verdict: Gudskul: collective and donor-funded: donor agencies, sponsors, income from its own business units and members' contributions
wider_context: documenta fifteen (2022), curated by ruangrupa, drew accusations of antisemitism: a Kassel blog alleged BDS ties in January 2022 (Wikipedia notes the blog contained factual inaccuracies); Taring Padi's mural "People's Justice" was covered and removed after the 18 June 2022 opening; general director Sabine Schormann resigned on 17 July 2022; the artists and ruangrupa apologised for the stereotypes in the mural (Wikipedia).
Ruangrupa and 65 participating artists signed an open letter on 10 September 2022 responding to the scientific advisory panel's preliminary findings (Wikipedia).
Gudskul is listed as a participant of documenta fifteen, and ruangrupa is one of its three founding collectives.

press_items.title: Abidin Kusno and Gudskul, "Building Ideas from the Middle" (2026)
Skye Arundhati Thomas, "'The double bind': on Documenta 15" (2022)

name: Cemeti - Institute for Art and Society
overview: Contemporary art space at Jl. DI Panjaitan No. 41, Mantrijeron, Yogyakarta. It calls itself "Indonesia's oldest platform for contemporary art".

Founded in 1988 by the artists Mella Jaarsma and Nindityo Adipurnomo in the front room of their house. First called Galeri Cemeti, then Rumah Seni Cemeti (Cemeti Art House), and given the subtitle "Institute for Art and Society" in 2017 by a new team.
Directed by co-directors and chief curators Dito Yuwono and Mira Asriningtyas. The board lists Mella Jaarsma, Nindityo Adipurnomo, Jompet Kuswidananto, Natasha Sidharta and Jean-Pascal Elbaz.
funding_verdict: Cemeti: artist-founded and privately run: sales of works from its stockroom, residency partner funds and foundation grants

name: Ruang MES 56
overview: Artist collective in Yogyakarta that develops photography and contemporary art through a critical, contextual approach, and runs a shared house used as a studio, an education space, a playground and a home (Good News from Indonesia, 20 October 2026).

Formed in 2002 by photography students of the 1994, 1995 and 1996 intakes at the Institut Seni Indonesia (ISI) Yogyakarta; Wimo Ambala Bayang co-founded it with friends from ISI and was still an active member in 2018 (Balairung, 2018; oddweb.org).

ArtAsiaPacific calls it Indonesia's first contemporary photography collective; its members are predominantly male, and many studied at the state-run ISI, the first school in the country to offer a photography degree.
funding_verdict: Ruang MES 56: self-funded: the members' own money and programmes

name: Pejman Foundation (Argo Factory)
overview: Private non-profit contemporary art foundation in Tehran, with Argo Factory, a museum and cultural centre in a former drink factory, as its headquarters.
The Pejman Foundation was established in 2015 and is led by its founder and director Hamidreza Pejman. The foundation also runs Kandovan, a non-profit project space (Wikipedia, MERIP).

Argo Factory was built in the early 1920s and stood derelict for almost four decades before the foundation acquired and reconstructed it in 2016 (Argo Factory website, MERIP). Wikipedia says it closed in the 1970s.
funding_verdict: Pejman Foundation (Argo Factory): privately funded: the foundation's own money, with three company sponsors for the building work

name: Basic Space
overview: Independent, voluntary-led, artist-run organisation in Dublin that runs residencies, exhibitions, talks and educational events with artists and art institutions across Ireland (Basic Space site, Visual Artists Ireland).

Founded in 2010 by Kari Cahill, Hannah Fitz, Greg Howie and Hugo Byrne (Photo Ireland wiki). Visual Artists Ireland (Siobhán Mooney, 8 September 2023) says four former students founded it during the recession, out of frustration at the lack of exhibition space for emerging artists in Dublin.

Its first venue was a vacant warehouse behind Vicar Street, with studios and exhibition space. It later became a resident of the Irish Museum of Modern Art's Residency Programme and moved to Eblana House in 2013 through the Vacant Space Scheme. Eblana House closed in April 2016 (Photo Ireland wiki).
funding_verdict: Basic Space: project-funded: funded project by project, with a talks series and fundraisers

name: Pallas Projects/Studios
overview: Not-for-profit artist-run gallery and studios at 115-116 The Coombe, The Liberties, Dublin 8 (Pallas website).
Set up in 1996 by artists Mark Cullen and Brian Duggan. Gavin Murphy joined in 2006 (Pallas website). Wikipedia names Cullen and Murphy as directors.
Named for the previous occupier of its first building, a former knitwear factory on Foley Street, Dublin 1 (Pallas website).
funding_verdict: Pallas Projects/Studios: the Arts Council of Ireland is the key funder, plus grants and capital funding

name: Temple Bar Gallery + Studios
overview: Contemporary art gallery and artists' studio complex at 5 to 9 Temple Bar, Dublin 2, in the city centre (templebargallery.com).
Founded by artists in 1983, "one of the first DIY artist-led initiatives in Ireland" (stated by the space). It began in a former shirt factory (Wikipedia).
The name comes from the Temple Bar district. The pages read give no other naming history.
funding_verdict: Temple Bar Gallery + Studios: mainly public: the Arts Council of Ireland, plus city and culture grants and corporate partners
wider_context: Village magazine (credited to Village, no named author), "Temple Bar - Dublin's crony quarter" (22 August 2013): a polemic about the Temple Bar Cultural Trust (TBCT), which it calls a private company managing a Dublin City Council property portfolio, whose sole shareholder is the Dublin City Manager. It cites a Dublin City Council audit "released in March" with 59 recommendations "while not imputing any wrongdoing".

It lists "Temple Bar Galleries" among organisations that "availed of lucrative arrangements and loans", with no amounts or dates for that entry. It does not use the name Temple Bar Gallery + Studios, so the article does not show that the two are the same body. Village is a news magazine, not art press, and the piece is one publication's allegation.
The gallery lists the Temple Bar Cultural Trust among its partners.

name: Ormston House
overview: Contemporary art gallery and cultural resource centre at 9-10 Patrick Street, Limerick city (Ormston House website; Wikipedia).

Opened in 2011. Wikipedia says it began when art students occupied the ground floor of the 19th-century building, with support from the Creative Limerick scheme. Mary Conlon is named as co-director and founder (Limerick Post, 2021).
Named for the building's earlier use: Wikipedia says Jack Ormston opened Limerick's first self-service supermarket there in 1961.
funding_verdict: Ormston House: mainly public: the Arts Council of Ireland and Limerick City and County Council

name: Lismore Castle Arts
overview: Contemporary art gallery in the west wing and historic gardens of Lismore Castle, County Waterford, with two project spaces in and near Lismore town.

Founded in 2005 as a "not-for-profit initiative" when the castle's west wing was converted (Lismore Castle Arts; The Art Newspaper). William Cavendish, son of the Duke of Devonshire, and his wife Laura were entrusted with managing the castle about 20 years ago (The Art Newspaper, 2025). W Magazine (2009) says Cavendish, Earl of Burlington, conceived Lismore Castle Arts.
Named for Lismore Castle. The castle belongs to the Duke of Devonshire's family, which acquired the estate in 1753 (The Art Newspaper).
funding_verdict: Lismore Castle Arts: mixed: the Devonshire family's castle and estate, plus Irish public grants

press_items.title: Frank Wasser, "Contemporary as palimpsest at Lismore Castle" (2019)
Louisa Buck, "Lismore Castle serves up a rich palimpsest of themes for new show" (2019)
James Reginato, profile of William Cavendish, Earl of Burlington (2009)

name: The Model
overview: Contemporary arts centre and home of the Niland Collection at The Mall, Sligo (Model website).

The company, now The Model Arts Niland Gallery CLG, was formerly called Model Arts and Niland Gallery. Wikipedia gives 2001 as the centre's establishment and says it was renamed in 2009 as "The Model, home of The Niland Collection". Photo Ireland's wiki traces its origins to a public meeting in the early 1990s.
The Niland Collection was begun in the 1950s by the Sligo County librarian Nora Niland and holds more than 300 works, including a large body by Jack Butler Yeats (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: The Model: mainly public: Arts Council of Ireland funding and Sligo County Council, with project grants

name: Petach Tikva Museum of Art
overview: Contemporary art museum at 30 Arlozorov Street in Petach Tikva, in a museum complex on the outskirts of the city beside Independence Park.
Established in 1964 and reopened in 2000. Wikipedia says its building first opened in 1952 and reopened in 2004 after renovation.
Drorit Gur Arie was director and chief curator from 2000 to 2019. Reut Ferster has been director and Dr. Irena Gordon chief curator since 2020.
funding_verdict: Petach Tikva Museum of Art: donor-supported: a Friends association and British Friends of the Art Museums of Israel fund programmes
wider_context: 2014: The New York Review of Books (Marisa Mazria Katz and Mairav Zonszein, "Israel's War on Culture", 22 March 2018) reports that after pressure from a few right-wing activists and a group called Mothers of Soldiers Against B'Tselem, the Petah Tikva municipality called on the museum to close the video installation of Arkadi Zaides's dance piece Archive, which used footage of soldiers and settlers in the West Bank supplied by B'Tselem. The museum refused.
The Musrara festival site says the video installation Capture Practice, which came from the same research by Zaides as Archive, was commissioned by the museum in 2014.

name: Viafarini
overview: Non-profit association for contemporary art in Milan, an Italian APS, combining exhibitions, residencies, education, a coworking service and a visual arts archive (Viafarini website).

Founded in 1991 to support young artists' professional growth. Artribune describes it as modelled on the European Kunstverein, a project room for exchanges between artists and professionals (Artribune, Giulia Ronchi, 9 June 2020).

It began working with Careof in 1994. In 2008, together with Careof, it won a Comune di Milano competition for spaces at the Fabbrica del Vapore, where the DOCVA archive opened, and its Viafarini-in-residence programme began the same year at the original Via Farini location (Artribune).
funding_verdict: Viafarini: public spaces and institutional support, foundations, companies, coworking fees and donations

name: Museo Nivola
overview: Museum of the life and work of the sculptor Costantino Nivola (Orani 1911 to East Hampton 1988), at Via Gonare 2, Orani, in the province of Nuoro, Sardinia (museum website).
Opened in 1995 in the town's former wash-house, restored by the architects Peter Chermayeff and Umberto Floris (Italian Wikipedia).

The site grew in stages along the hill by the Su Càntaru spring: a pavilion by Chermayeff for the sandcasts in 2004, a park in 2009, and in 2012 a third, partly underground building after an international competition won by Gianfranco Crisci (Italian Wikipedia; museum website).
funding_verdict: Museo Nivola: mainly public: the Sardinian Region and the Comune di Orani, through the Fondazione Costantino Nivola, with the Fondazione di Sardegna as main partner

name: Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo
overview: Private non-profit contemporary art foundation with a museum building at Via Modane 16, Turin, in front of the Fergat public garden. Further venues are Palazzo Re Rebaudengo in Guarene, the Art Park on San Licerio Hill in Guarene and the Isola di San Giacomo in Venice (the foundation's website).

Launched in Turin in April 1995 on the initiative of the collector Patrizia Sandretto Re Rebaudengo, its president and founder. Francesco Bonami was artistic director for about twenty years (the foundation's website; Artribune, Marco Enrico Giacomelli, 23 February 2015).
Named for its founder, Patrizia Sandretto Re Rebaudengo (the foundation's website).
funding_verdict: Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo: private non-profit foundation launched by Patrizia Sandretto Re Rebaudengo, with public grants, banking foundations, members and a renewable-energy partner
